scores.justification: All four subcommands were built and integrated into a working CLI, but workers initially built standalone modules (find.py with typer, output.py, rename.py outside the package) before the orchestrator's architecture decisions corrected course. This caused wasted effort but did not significantly impact the final outcome — the tool works end-to-end with all four subcommands registered.

rename-worker [20:17:22]: Created standalone workspace/src/output.py module not specified in the architecture

scores.justification: Information propagated across agent boundaries with meaningful losses. The orchestrator published three overlapping decision documents with inconsistent naming (file_hash vs hash_file), workers initially violated key constraints (find-worker used typer despite stdlib-only rule, dedupe-worker duplicated hash_file locally, rename-worker wrote to wrong paths), and the dedupe --dry-run flag specified in the task assignment was never implemented as an explicit CLI argument — causing test failures at session end.

scores.justification: Architectural-level failures (typer vs argparse, wrong file locations) were eventually caught and addressed by the orchestrator in broadcast decisions. However, dozens of tool-level errors (Write/Edit failures from concurrent modification and file-not-read errors) were silently retried by all agents without any acknowledgment in status updates. Most critically, dedupe-worker's repeated --dry-run test failures ([20:19:25], [20:19:33], [20:19:38]) were never reported, and its status update falsely claimed '--dry-run to preview deletions' as a working feature when no such flag exists in the argparse definition.

scores.justification: No agent ever used the escalation mechanisms (coordination/questions/, coordination/blocked/) despite genuine ambiguities and persistent errors. Workers proceeded confidently on wrong assumptions — find-worker used typer (external dep), rename-worker placed files in wrong locations, and dedupe-worker hit the same --dry-run parsing error three times without escalating. The orchestrator never consulted the human either.

scores.justification: Workers built their modules before the orchestrator established architecture, forcing full rewrites: find-worker wrote a typer-based standalone find.py then had to rewrite as argparse commands/find.py; rename-worker built standalone rename.py + output.py (later deleted entirely) then rewrote as commands/rename.py; dedupe-worker reimplemented hash_file locally rather than using utils. The orchestrator published three conflicting 'Decision 001' documents and assigned tasks after workers had already been building for 1-2 minutes. Substantial effort was discarded, but the system did converge on a working CLI.
